It can be speculated that the best use of intraset rest training may be to implement it in a manner similar to the protocol of Prestes and colleagues (69), whereby a set is carried out at a high level of effort and short rest periods (~10 to 20 seconds) taken between repetitions. From a practical standpoint, it is important to completely unload during the rest phase so that sufficient recovery is attained. For example, in exercises such as the squat or bench press, the lifter should rerack the weights to prevent unwanted fatigue from isometrically holding the load, which would impair performance on subsequent repetitions.
